processing: Orthodox tea from the season's first tender leaves, rolled by hand or machine. As with Darjeeling first flush, oxidation is generally kept light, which explains the pale cup.
harvest_season: Begins in the fourth week of March and runs to the end of April.
appearance_dry: Typical of spring orthodox tea: wiry, mixed green and brown leaf with some pale tips.
appearance_liquor: Light yellowish green, closer to a green tea than to a typical black.
appearance_wet: Tender, bright leaf with a greenish cast, as is usual for spring pickings.
taste_profile: Delicate, with a subtle aroma and flavour. Floral, fresh notes are what to expect by analogy with Darjeeling first flush.

brewing.notes: General guidance for delicate spring black teas. Use water off the boil and no milk; hot water and long steeps turn it sharp.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year as the spring crop, generally arriving after the April picking ends. It is the costliest flush because little is made and demand exceeds supply. As with other first flush teas, freshness is the point, so buy the current year and finish it within about a year.
description:
This is the first orthodox picking of the year in Nepal's hills, taken from late March through April. The leaf is tender, the cup pale, and it is the closest Nepal comes to the character people pay for in Darjeeling first flush.

Little is written about this flush as a separate tea, so most processing details follow its class: a gentle treatment that keeps the leaf fresh. Technically it is sold as black tea, though the yellow-green liquor will not look it.

Delicate is the key word. Use cooler water than you would for other black teas and a short steep, and skip the milk, which would bury it.

Look for the estate or district, usually in eastern Nepal, and the picking year. Price is high for the region, because supply is small.
history: Little is documented about this flush in its own right. It belongs to Nepal's orthodox tea, which grew out of the hill estates of Ilam, the first of them set up around 1863, and the four-flush calendar it shares with Darjeeling.
